questions.stem: What is Partitioning in a database?
options: Copying a table to several servers for redundancy
Compressing a table so it occupies fewer blocks
A data organisation scheme in which table data is divided across multiple storage objects called data partitions according to values in one or more columns
Splitting a database into separate schemas per department
Assigning each table to a dedicated node in a shared-nothing cluster
questions.explanation: Partitioning divides a table's data into separately stored data partitions based on the values in one or more table columns.

questions.stem: What does each data partition consist of?
options: Its own data, indexes, configuration files and transaction logs
Only the rows, with indexes held centrally
A read-only snapshot of the parent table
Just a pointer to the original table
Data and indexes, but no logs
questions.explanation: Each partition is stored separately and consists of its data, indexes, configuration files and transaction logs.

questions.stem: If a Salary table holding 10 years of data is partitioned yearly, how is it divided at the storage level?
options: Into 2 datasets, one for current and one for historical data
Into 120 datasets, one per month
Into one dataset per employee
Into 10 smaller datasets, one for each year
Into 10 datasets each holding a copy of all years
questions.explanation: Yearly partitioning of 10 years of salary data produces 10 smaller datasets, one per year.

questions.stem: When partitions are stored wherever empty slots exist, so that several partitions may land on one node of a cluster, what is this arrangement called?
options: Shared-nothing architecture
Shared architecture
Sharded architecture
Vertical architecture
Composite architecture
questions.explanation: Storing partitions in whatever empty slots are available, possibly several on one node, is called Shared Architecture.

questions.stem: In the yearly Salary example, a query for years 2 and 3 hits only two partitions, but both sit on the same node. What is the consequence?
options: The query fails because partitions must be on separate nodes
All 10 nodes process the query in parallel
The query reads all 10 partitions anyway
The partitions are moved to separate nodes before the query runs
The query is faster than a full scan, but only one node's processing power is used
questions.explanation: Hitting just two partitions makes the query much faster, but as both are on one node only that node's processing is used.

options: Placing entire columns into new, distinct tables
Separating one table's rows into multiple partitions that share the same schema and columns but hold entirely different rows
Storing each partition on a dedicated node
Combining several small tables into one large table
Splitting a table by the data type of its columns
questions.explanation: Horizontal partitioning splits rows into multiple tables, each with the same schema and columns but different rows.

options: Dividing rows by a date range
Distributing rows using a hash function
Hashing the primary key to select a node
Separating entire columns into new, distinct tables whose data is independent of the others
Splitting rows into partitions with identical columns
questions.explanation: In vertical partitioning entire columns are separated into new tables, each holding distinct rows and columns independent of the others.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a single-level partitioning technique?
options: Range–Hash Partitioning
Hash Partitioning
Range Partitioning
List Partitioning
Single-level Hash Partitioning
questions.explanation: Single-level techniques are Hash, Range and List partitioning; Range–Hash is a composite technique.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a composite partitioning technique?
options: Hash Partitioning
Range Partitioning
List Partitioning
Vertical Partitioning
List–Hash Partitioning
questions.explanation: Composite techniques combine two methods, such as Range–Range, Range–Hash, Range–List, List–Range, List–Hash and List–List.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a stated benefit of partitioning?
options: Queries can be solved for a collection of partitions instead of a giant database
Planned downtime is reduced
It eliminates the need for backups
Parallel execution optimises resource utilisation and shortens execution time
Administration tasks such as loading, index creation and backup can be done at the partition level
questions.explanation: Partitioning makes backup and recovery faster at the partition level, but it does not remove the need for backups.
